name: HDFC Life Insurance Company Ltd
title: HDFC Life Insurance Company Ltd - 540777 - Transcript Of Earnings Conference Call - FY'26

read.thesis: FY26 VNB up only 2% to INR 4,034 crores with margin at 24.2% (25.5% ex-GST/SSV); management says growth and VNB to lag, and is not chasing margin, with counter share at HDFC Bank slipping from mid-60s to early-60s.

capex.peers_comment: Management described aggressive pricing and underwriting by competitors in the bank channel, without capacity terms.
capex.quote: Really on competition on price point, we don't believe that that is sustainable on a long-term basis, whether it's aggression on pricing and/or on underwriting.

triggers.label: Bank-channel price aggression, counter share down
triggers.quote: The counter share in HDFC Bank in Q4 was lower than what it was in 9 months.

triggers.label: No APE/VNB number for FY27
triggers.quote: rather than trying to put a number, because a number means that you're going invest resources and so on up front.

triggers.label: GST margin drag 300bps → 110bps
triggers.quote: We started with 300 basis points, brought it down to 190 and now we are standing at 110 basis points.

triggers.label: Protection growth 43%, Q4 46%
triggers.quote: Protection was a clear highlight during the year, with a growth of 43%

guidance.value: not prioritised; VNB growth in line with APE first
guidance.quote: Are we in a tearing rush to get to that at the cost of growth? We are not.
by the time we finish the first half of next year, we should be done with the GST impact

guidance.value: grow faster than industry; VNB growth in line with APE
guidance.quote: Our aspiration to outpace industry new business and VNB growth remains unchanged.

prior_guidance_check.quote: FY26 closed below our original expectation.
the headwind on margins has been moderating in line with our guidance

red_flags.label: VNB +2% vs APE +7%; FY23-26 VNB CAGR ~3%
red_flags.quote: I am looking at FY26 number, your CAGR has been just 3%, FY26 over FY23.

red_flags.label: Persistency deterioration 13th month down 200bps
red_flags.quote: On persistency, the 13th month ratio moderated by 200 basis points during the year

red_flags.label: Dividend paid alongside INR 1,000cr equity raise
red_flags.quote: we have taken board approval to raise up to INR1,000 crores by way of a preferential issue to our parent

evasions.topic: Bank channel share outlook and pricing
evasions.quote: conversations are not only around share because the share is in an open architecture platform
this is growth capital, no different from any other sector

summary.headline: HDFC Life FY26 VNB rose only 2% to INR 4,034 crores; NBM fell to 24.2% after GST and surrender-value impacts, with Q4 growth slowing at HDFC Bank.
summary.overview: FY26 individual APE grew 7% YoY, but top-line growth fell below the company's original expectation, with the slowdown concentrated in Q4 from unabsorbed GST, softer bancassurance and deferred demand in March. Proprietary channels grew 15-16% in Q4 and FY26, and protection grew 43% for the year. VNB rose 2% to INR 4,034 crores and NBM fell 140 bps to 24.2%, with 130 bps from GST/SSV, 90 bps from fixed-cost absorption, and 40 bps from persistency assumption strengthening, partly offset by 120 bps of product mix. Management said the GST drag is tapering (about 110 bps in Q4) and should be neutralised by H1 FY27.

financial_highlights.metric: New business margin excl. GST and SSV

financial_highlights.change: 16% growth excl. GST and labour code impact

financial_highlights.value: INR 2.10 per share, INR 456 crores total payout

segments.name: Individual APE mix FY26
segments.commentary: Unit-linked 44%, non-par savings 18%, participating 25%, term 7% (vs 5% in FY25), annuity 5%. Management expects non-par to regain share in FY27.

segments.name: Retail protection
segments.commentary: Grew 43% in FY26 and 46% in Q4; retail protection mix rose about 200 bps to 7.2%, and about 10% including riders. Around 80% of post-GST protection buyers are new to HDFC Life.

segments.name: Annuity
segments.commentary: Mix rose about 300 bps YoY to around 8% of individual APE in Q4; AGNI, a variable annuity linked to Nifty 50, launched in Q4 at a ticket size of INR 25 lakh and above.

segments.name: Agency channel
segments.commentary: Grew about 500 bps ahead of the company; over 250 branches added in 30 months contribute about 13% of agency top line. FC base grew 43% gross.

segments.name: Partnership / HDFC Bank channel
segments.commentary: Counter share in Q4 was below the 9-month level and closed FY26 in the early 60s% vs mid-60s% last year. Management stepped back from unviable business; HDFC Bank contributes about 40% of NBP.

segments.name: Credit protect
segments.commentary: MFI business grew about 13% for the full year; Q4 MFI growth exceeded 40% on a subdued base.

segments.name: Subsidiaries
segments.commentary: HDFC Pension Fund Management has a 43% market share and AUM above INR 1.5 lakh crore.

guidance_outlook: GST margin headwind fell from 300 bps to 190 bps to 110 bps in Q4; management expects it to be largely neutralised by end of H1 FY27.

FY27 priority is growth faster than industry with VNB growth in line with APE growth; management said it is not chasing the 25.5% margin at the cost of growth, but margin expansion is on the table over three years.
No numerical FY27 APE or VNB guidance given; management said it will plan a month at a time.
Solvency: INR 1,000 crore preferential issue to HDFC Bank adds about 900 bps; a further INR 500 crore sub-debt would add about 400 bps, for about 1,300-1,400 bps in total.
Ind AS forbearance to be sought for FY27, with full adoption targeted for FY28; the risk-based capital transition timeline remains unclear.
capex_capacity: Over 250 branches added in the last 30 months; focus shifting from expansion to productivity, activation and branch-level profitability.
Branches in smaller markets expected to take about 1.5x longer to reach productivity than metro branches, per management.
Rider APE now at least 5x-6x the level of a year and a half ago (below 1% of unit-linked premium then); about one-quarter of unit-linked sales carry higher sum assured.
Participating fund in deficit after GST and surrender-value reserve changes; company plans to contribute back to par FFA over the next couple of years.
demand_pricing: Competition in the HDFC Bank channel is driven by aggressive pricing and underwriting. Management says it has stepped back from loss-making cohorts and will not match outlier IRRs on non-par.
Non-par demand was softer than expected; management said pricing discipline and product refinements (Click 2 Achieve series) are underway for FY27 as the yield curve improves.
Unit-linked demand remained resilient through FY26, with higher protection multiples and better rider attachment.
Management said it had 'taken a back seat' in some protection and non-par segments, such as low sum assured multiple unit-linked and short-pay products, where economics did not work.

qa_highlights.question: How has counter share in HDFC Bank changed in Q4 vs the nine months, and what gives confidence it will normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 counter share was lower than the 9-month level; FY26 closed in the early 60s% vs mid-60s% prior year. Management says it knows which cohorts it let go and what it takes to compete back, and expects to regain share as GST costs are absorbed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the participating fund in deficit and why is new business strain rising faster?
qa_highlights.answer: Deficit reflects GST ITC loss on renewal commission and maintenance expenses, plus higher surrender-value reserves from October 2024 regulation changes. Strain rose because of protection and credit protect growth, higher ULIP multiples and rider attachment, and GST impact.

qa_highlights.question: Can VNB grow in line with the 2023 plan, and what is the normalised three-year VNB CAGR?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says FY23-FY26 CAGR was about 3%; adjusting for roughly INR 1,000 crore of GST and SSV effects, the normalised three-year VNB CAGR would be about 9-10%. Management expects a 1.8x-2x growth over four years to remain the aim.

qa_highlights.question: Why did persistency assumption changes and the yield-curve movement not show up separately in the VNB walk?
qa_highlights.answer: Economic assumption changes are captured within product profile rather than shown separately, since repricing is dynamic. Persistency sensitivity rose because ULIP mix increased and surrender-value rules now affect non-linked margins.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company expand to deeper markets, and what are the returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says Tier 2 and 3 is a priority, with customers acquired in FY26 over 72% new to HDFC Life and Tier 2/3 growing faster than Tier 1. Payback is about 1.5x longer than metro branches.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the dividend maintained when a INR 1,000 crore preferential issue is planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the capital is growth capital for protection, the dividend is business as usual for retail and pension shareholders, and the company balanced both objectives by keeping the payout flat.

risks_watch: HDFC Bank counter share: management said Q4 share fell below the 9-month level; monitor whether it recovers in FY27.
Persistency: 13th month ratio fell about 200 bps in FY26 and assumptions were strengthened; Q4 trend stabilised, but sensitivity has risen with ULIP mix.
Competitive intensity and possible commission regulation, which management said it is watching.
Timing of the risk-based capital (RBC) regime and Ind AS forbearance; RBC is expected after the IFRS rollout.
Non-par volumes remain weak; recovery depends on yield-curve support and product refinements.
summary.management_tone: Confident on protection, agency and the medium-term margin path, but cautious and somewhat evasive on FY27 growth; management declined to give an APE or VNB number and pointed to HDFC Bank counter-share competition as a short-term issue.
key_quotes: Protection was a clear highlight during the year, with a growth of 43% supported by lower prices post-GST and a strengthened product portfolio.
On GST, the headwind on margins has been moderating in line with our guidance.
So, the one-off is actually only one-off; it's only one-time impact on the existing book.
Are we in a tearing rush to get to that at the cost of growth? We are not.

adds.what: Over 250 branches added in the last 30 months (focus now shifting to productivity, not further expansion)

growth.why: No numerical FY27 APE or VNB guidance, but management aims to grow faster than industry with VNB growth in line with APE, and says the GST margin drag should be neutralised by H1 FY27; backing is partial (protection growth, rider and annuity launches, Click 2 Achieve refinements) with no specific capacity or order numbers.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.when: H1 FY27 onward; GST drag neutralised by H1 FY27
rows.why: GST headwind fell from 300 bps to 190 bps to 110 bps in Q4 and management expects it neutralised by H1 FY27, while NBM excl. GST and SSV was flat at 25.5% vs 25.6%; management says margin expansion is on the table over three years but not prioritised over growth.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Over 250 branches were added in 30 months and focus is shifting from expansion to productivity and branch-level profitability; no new capacity figures were given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Individual APE grew 7% in FY26 with proprietary channels up 15-16% and protection up 43%, and management aims to grow faster than industry with VNB growth in line with APE, though no numerical FY27 APE guidance was given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex and utilisation were not discussed; the only capital action is a INR 1,000 crore preferential issue to HDFC Bank plus a possible INR 500 crore sub-debt, which is solvency and growth capital rather than physical capacity.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numerical FY27 APE or VNB guidance was given, management plans month by month, and HDFC Bank counter share fell below the 9-month level in Q4 (FY26 closed in early 60s% vs mid-60s%).

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Top-line growth fell below the company's original expectation with Q4 slowing from unabsorbed GST and softer bancassurance, and bank counter share is down from mid-60s% to early 60s%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management plans Click 2 Achieve non-par refinements for FY27 as the yield curve improves, and AGNI (Nifty-linked variable annuity) launched in Q4 at INR 25 lakh+ ticket size, with non-par expected to regain share.

rows.label: HDFC Bank counter share recovery
rows.why: Counter share fell to early 60s% from mid-60s% last year and Q4 was below the 9-month level, but management expects to regain share as GST costs are absorbed.

rows.label: GST drag tapering to neutralisation
rows.why: The GST margin headwind fell from 300 bps to 190 bps to 110 bps in Q4, and management expects it largely neutralised by end of H1 FY27.

rows.label: Solvency uplift from capital raise
rows.why: INR 1,000 crore preferential issue to HDFC Bank adds about 900 bps and a further INR 500 crore sub-debt about 400 bps, taking solvency from 177% to roughly 1,300-1,400 bps higher in total.

tone.note: Management was confident on protection (up 43%), agency and the medium-term margin path, but cautious on FY27 growth and declined to give APE or VNB numbers; analysts pushed on HDFC Bank counter-share loss, persistency, and why new business strain is rising.
